rules.title: Santa Ana algorithmic rent-setting software ordinance
rules.requirement: Prohibits the sale, licensing, provision and use of certain algorithmic rent-setting software for residential rental property in Santa Ana. Tenants may sue directly and need only prove the landlord used the prohibited technology, not intentional collusion.
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation
rules.penalty: Tenant may seek injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, plus attorney's fees.
rules.citation: Santa Ana algorithmic rent-setting software ordinance (no number given)
rules.status_basis: Approved for first reading Feb. 17, 2026; final vote set for March 3, 2026; the text does not report final adoption.

requires.name: residential_rental_property
requires.text: limited to residential rental property within Santa Ana city limits

exempt_if.name: public_or_aggregate_data_software
exempt_if.text: pricing software that relies solely on publicly available data, aggregate historical data

exempt_if.name: affordable_housing_compliance_tools
exempt_if.text: tools used to comply with affordable housing program requirements

coverage.summary: Applies to residential rental property within Santa Ana city limits.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Does not apply to pricing software relying solely on public or aggregate historical data, or tools used to comply with affordable housing programs.

precedence.text: It is structured to operate alongside existing and proposed state antitrust laws while providing stronger local protections.

rules.quoted_span: The ordinance, approved on Tuesday, Feb. 17, for a first reading and set for a final vote on March 3, prohibits the sale, licensing, provision and use of certain algorithmic rent-setting software for residential rental properties.
